questions.question: A, B and C can complete a work in x, 30 and 45 days, respectively. B and C worked together for 6 days. The remaining work was completed by A alone in 12 days. The value of x is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken to complete the work by A = x days

Time taken to complete the work by B = 30 days

Time taken to complete the work by C = 45 days

Time taken to complete the work by B and C together = 6 days

Remaining work completed by A = 12 days

**Formula used:**

Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculation:**

LCM of 30 and 45 is 90

Efficiency of B = 90/30 = 3 units/day

Efficiency of C = 90/45 = 2 units/day

Total units of work by B and C together = [(3 + 2) × 6]

⇒ 30 units

Efficiency of B and C together = (90 – 30) = 60 units

Efficiency of A = (60/12) = 5 units/day

Hence, A can complete the whole work in = (90/5) days

⇒ x = 18 days

**∴ The value of x is 18**

questions.question: Two cars X and Y start running towards each other from two places 216 km apart. The ratio of the speeds of X and Y is 5 ∶ 7 and the speed of X is 60 km/h. After how many minutes will X and Y meet each other?
questions.solution:

X and Y start running towards each other from two places = 216 km

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance/Speed

1 hr = 60 min

**Calculation:**

Let the ratio of speed of X and Y be 5x and 7x respectively

According to the question

⇒ 5x = 60

⇒ x = 12

Then,

Speed of Y = 7x = (7 × 12) = 84 km/h

Now,

Time = [216/(60 + 84)]

⇒ (216/144)

⇒ 1.5 Hour = (1.5 × 60) min

⇒ 90 min

**∴ Time taken to meet X and Y is 90**

questions.question: The average weight of some students in a group is 58 kg. If 8 students of average weight 54 kg leave the group, and 3 students weighing 53.6 kg, 54 kg and 57.4 kg join the group, then the average weight of the remaining students in the group will increase by 575 g. The number of students, initially, in the group is
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average weight of some students = 58 kg

Weight of 8 students who leave the group = 54 kg

Number of three students who joined the group = 53.6, 54 and 57.4 kg

Average weight of the remaining students increase = 575 g

**Formula used:**

Average = sum of observations/Number of observations

**Calculation:**

Let the number of students be x

According to the question

⇒ [(58 × x) – (8 × 54) + (53.6 + 54 + 57.4)] = (x – 8 + 3) (58 + 0.575)

⇒ 58x – 432 + 165 = (x – 5) (58.575)

⇒ 58x – 267 = (58.575x – 292.875)

⇒ (58.575x – 58x) = (292.875 – 267)

⇒ 0.575x = 25.875

⇒ x = (25.875/0.575)

⇒ x = 45

**∴ The number of the students in the group is 45**

questions.question: The price of an article increases by 5% every year. If the difference between its price at the end of the second and the third year is Rs. 52.50, then what will be its price at the end of the first year?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__** Let the starting price be 100 units.

Price after one year = 100 + 5 = 105 units

Price after second year = 105 + (105 × 5)/100 = 110.25 units

Price after third year = 110.25 + (110.25 × 5)/100 = 115.7625 units

According to the question,

115.7625 - 110.2500 = 52.50

⇒ 5.5125 units = 52.50

⇒ 1 unit = 9.5238

⇒ 100 units = 952.38

⇒ 105 units = 1000

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__****Given:**

The price of an article increases = 5%

The difference between its price at the end of the second and third year = Rs. 52.50

**Calculation:**

Let the initial price be 10000x

Price at the end of the first year = (10000x × 105/100) = 10500x

Price at the end of the second year = (10500x × 105/100) = 11025x

Price at the end of the third year = (11025x × 105/100) = 11576.25x

According to the question

⇒ 11576.25x – 11025x = 52.50

⇒ 551.25x = 52.50

⇒ x = 52.50/551.25

⇒ x = 0.0952

Price at the end of the first year = 10500x = (10500 × 0.0952)

⇒ Rs. 999.6 ~ Rs. 1000

**∴ Required first year price is Rs. 1000.**

questions.question: A man buys goods for Rs. 8,000. He sells 30% of those goods at a profit of 12% and 40% of the remaining goods at a profit of 25%. At what profit percentage should he sell the remaining goods to gain 30% in the entire transaction (correct to one decimal place)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost price of goods = Rs. 8000

**Formula used:**

Profit = SP – CP

Profit% = Profit/CP × 100

**Calculation:**

According to the question

30%of goods = (8000 × 30/100)

⇒ Rs. 2400

Profit = 12%

SP = (2400 × 112/100)

⇒ Rs. 2688

CP of 40% of remaining goods = (8000 – 2400) = Rs. 5600

⇒ (5600 × 40/100)

⇒ Rs. 2240

CP of 40% of remaining goods = Rs. 2240

Profit = 25%

SP = (2240 × 125/100)

⇒ Rs. 2800

He has to gain 30% on whole transaction

SP = (8000 × 130/100)

⇒ Rs. 10400

CP left = [8000 – (2400 + 2240)

⇒ (8000 – 4640)

⇒ Rs. 3360

SP left = [10400 – (2688 + 2800)]

⇒ (10400 – 5488)

⇒ Rs. 4912

Profit ended on remaining goods = Rs. (4912 – 3360)

⇒ Rs. 1552

Profit% = (1552/3360 × 100)

⇒ Rs.(155,200/3360)

⇒ 46.2%

**∴ Required profit percentage is 46.2%**

questions.question: The six-digit number 537xy5 is divisible by 125. How many such six-digit numbers are there?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The six digit numbers = 537xy5

**Concept used:**

**Divisibility rule of 125:** The number formed by the hundred, tens and units digit of the number must be divisible by 125

**Calculation:**

If we multiply last 3 digit number with the even number i.e. 2, 4, 6 and 8 we get 0 at the last digit

which is not possible. 

So, we can multiply last three digit number by odd number 

We need the last digit to be 5

⇒ 125 × 1 = 125 (acceptable)

⇒ 125 × 2 = 250

⇒ 125 × 3 = 375 (acceptable)

⇒ 125 × 4 = 500

⇒ 125 × 5 = 625 (acceptable)

⇒ 125 × 6 = 750

⇒ 125 × 7 = 875 (acceptable)

⇒ 125 × 8 = 1000

We cannot multiply (125 × 9 = 1125) because it has three-digit units

So,

⇒ 12, 37, 62, 87 are the 4 values of x and y that are the possible cases

**∴ There are 4 such digit six-digit numbers**
